faq.q: Do I need experience to start?
faq.a: No. Most people who start with Cora have never done a structured program before. Sessions begin with an assessment of what you can already do, and the plan is built from there — not from a template.

faq.q: I've never touched a barbell — is strength training realistic for me?
faq.a: Yes. The first block is entirely about technique: how to brace, how to move the bar, how to fail a rep safely. Loading comes after the pattern is solid, not before.

faq.q: I've never run more than a mile. Is a 5K actually realistic?
faq.a: For almost everyone, yes — on a run/walk progression that adds distance gradually. The plan is built around your current mileage, not a generic couch-to-5K calendar.

faq.q: When can I start training after having a baby?
faq.a: Whenever your provider clears you for exercise — that clearance always comes first, no exceptions. After that, the plan starts with the basics: breath, core, and pelvic floor, before any loaded movement returns.

faq.q: Is it too late to start strength training in my 50s or 60s?
faq.a: No — it's one of the highest-value times to start. Exercises are chosen for joint-friendly ranges of motion first, and progress is measured in how you move through your week, not just numbers on a bar.
See the Packages section above — pricing is flat and posted, no quote required. Sessions are billed as you go; there's no long-term contract.

faq.q: Do you train in person or online?
faq.a: Both. In-person sessions are based in Eagle, Idaho; online programming works from anywhere with a phone and a lifting app.
24 hours' notice to reschedule a session at no charge. Life happens — a late cancel isn't the end of the world, but the slot can't always be backfilled on short notice.
